subject: POC next steps — observation strategy & success checklist
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@medaxis.com>, Michael Turner <michael.turner@medaxis.com>
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap and proposed POC success criteria

Hi Samantha / Michael —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and a proposed, minimal POC plan so we can lock timelines this week. Please confirm items below or flag changes.

High-level goal
- Validate model accuracy on MedAxis triage intents and measure latency at 95th percentile for your catalog (slots 1-20k daily).

Proposed success criteria (short list)
- Precision@top1 on curated validation set >= 88%
- False positive rate for urgent intent <= 3%
- 95th percentile latency < 350 ms in your region under steady-state load
- No PII leakage on sampled logs (we will provide redaction / KMS options)

POC modalities and timeline (suggested)
1) Week 1 (shadow): 2-week online shadow running against a 5% traffic slice, real-time logs but no live writes. This gives end-to-end latency and behavior under production traffic.
2) Week 2-3 (offline eval): run the same prompts offline against held-out datasets and the rubric below to measure precision and regression.
3) Week 4 (joint review and acceptance): reconcile differences, run the acceptance checklist, and decide go/no-go.

Ownership
- Redwood: model serving, KV cache config, telemetry dashboards, and the acceptance checklist template (attached).
- MedAxis: provide labelled validation set (ideally 1k-3k samples), a PO for 4 weeks of dedicated/dev capacity, and an internal owner for weekly syncs.

Attachments: redwood-poc-scope.pdf (scope and SOW), medaxis-magic-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (initial acceptance checklist stub)

Next steps
- Samantha: confirm that success criteria match your internal goals and whether the 2-week shadow is acceptable.
- Michael / procurement: high-level PO timing estimate.
- We propose kickoff Wednesday 26 Aug if accepted.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@medaxis.com>

Cc: Michael Turner <michael.turner@medaxis.com>, procurement@medaxis.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:41:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and proposed POC success criteria

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our side before we sign off:

1) Metrics priority: our primary focus is reducing triage errors for urgent cases. If we had to pick two metrics, it would be Precision@top1 and FP rate for urgent intent. Latency is important but secondary as long as it stays under ~400ms.
2) Data: we can provide a labelled set of ~1,200 examples. We will need guidance on formatting and a secure upload link.
3) Shadow vs offline: can you outline what we should expect in terms of risk for the shadow run? Are there mitigation steps if a model response is clearly wrong?

Michael (cc) — procurement would like to understand expected spend for the 4-week window and whether a short-term credit is available for the shadow portion.

Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Product Operations | MedAxis Health
samantha@medaxis.com

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap and proposed POC success criteria (technical notes)

Jonas / Marissa — a couple of implementation notes to address Samantha's questions and to make the plan runnable. This is internal only.

Short answers
- Shadow risk: low if we enforce response gating and live-only logs (no writes). We recommend the following mitigations:
  - Response tagging: add a header that marks any model output that falls below the confidence threshold.
  - Auto-fallback: route flagged cases to a safe default and surface as an event in the dashboard.
  - Rate-limited rollout: start with 1% traffic and ramp to 5% over 48–72 hours.

Offline vs Online grading rubric (draft)
- Offline (gold set): human-labelled set; measure Precision@1, Recall for urgent intents, and token-level hallucination check. Weight: 60% of the final score.
- Online shadow: live traffic but non-blocking; measure 95th pctl latency, confidence distribution, and adverse event rate. Weight: 40% of the final score.
- Passing threshold: combined weighted score >= 85% with no single metric failing catastrophic thresholds (e.g., FP urgent > 5%).

Owner matrix (suggested)
- Redwood SE (Ava): set up shadow pipeline, confidence tagging, dashboards, and redaction pipeline.
- Redwood AE (Jonas): commercial owner, weekly stakeholder syncs, acceptance gate decision.
- MedAxis Product (Samantha): provide labelled data, define clinical acceptance on edge cases, and approve final acceptance.

Attachments for internal review: medaxis-magic-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (v0.2 with rubric notes)

I'll update the checklist with the weighting table and share back to the external thread after we align.

--
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com

Samantha / Michael — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on your reply and Ava's notes, here's the finalized plan. Please confirm by end of day tomorrow so we can lock the kickoff.

Finalized plan (summary)- Scope: 4-week POC combining staged online shadow (weeks 1-2) and offline evaluation (weeks 2-3), joint acceptance in week 4.
- Acceptance scoring: weighted offline 60% / online 40%; pass >=85% combined and FP urgent <=3%.
- Risk mitigations: tagging + auto-fallback + 1% -> 5% ramp profile.
- Deliverables: redwood-poc-scope.pdf, medaxis-magic-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (attached).

Proposed schedule- Wed 26 Aug: kickoff and data handoff (Samantha to provide upload link by kickoff)
- Fri 5 Sep: mid-POC sync and early metrics
- Tue 14 Sep: acceptance review and decision

Commercial notes- Estimated spend for 4 weeks (shadow + evaluation): USD 18k–25k depending on actual traffic slice. Marissa will follow with a formal quote.
- We can offer a 1-week free shadow credit to reduce initial cost; procurement, please confirm PO timing.

Next steps
- Samantha: confirm data upload method and approval for ramp profile.
- Michael / procurement: rough PO timing and whether a one-week credit is acceptable.
- Marissa: send formal quote and draft order form.

Attachments: medaxis-magic-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (final v0.3), redwood-poc-scope.pdf

Looking forward to getting started.

Best,
